analysis.title: Global Macro Thoughts: Global Macro Themes (2 November 2026)
key_insights: Last week's tech sell-off was mainly sparked by Google and Intel earnings. MSFT earnings had calmed nerves early in the week, with revenue and EPS above consensus and Azure growth of 48%, above market expectations, with free cash flow staying positive.

Google was partly hit by concern that AI is eroding its search business. Google Cloud revenue growth was very strong, but capex projections kept rising and negative free cash flow was over $9bn, far worse than market expectations.

INTC EPS beat consensus, but Q4 guidance was $15-16bn revenue and $0.25 adjusted EPS against consensus of $17.1bn and $0.43. AMZN AWS revenue grew at its fastest pace in five years but EPS missed consensus, and trailing-12m free cash flow swung from positive to a negative of over $42bn.
The Nasdaq Composite is down over 6% in the past month, with GOOG down 19%, META down 15% and NVDA down over 10%. It is the Nasdaq's third correction of 2026, after March and July.

The move is a rotation out of tech rather than a broad pullback. The S&P 500 is down about 2% over the month and about 5% off its record high, while the equal-weighted S&P is up about 5% in October. Investors sold crowded AI trades and bought cyclicals, healthcare, defense and energy.

Barclays expects midterm results to have very limited macro impact. The 10y UST moved just 1-2bp the day after the 2014, 2018 and 2022 midterms, and each of those produced divided government, which looks likely again.

Prediction markets strongly expect Democrats to win the House and, by a small majority, the Senate. With a Republican President, Barclays sees limited macro impact from a Democratic Senate, and thinks new fiscal stimulus is unlikely with a Democratic Congress.

Barclays says election effects will be swamped by Qualcomm and AMD earnings and Friday's payrolls. It also calls concerns about nationwide data center bans far-fetched given the President's support for AI.

The Fed held rates as expected. Chair Warsh said inflation remains 'too high' and acknowledged that financial conditions have tightened a bit without calling them tight. Barclays expects hikes in December and January, followed by a prolonged hold, and sees December as live for the Fed, ECB and BoJ.

Barclays does not see the recent weeks as the start of an AI collapse. Previous tech cycles collapsed when supply overwhelmed demand, but last week's message was that compute demand still outpaces supply. Bull markets usually end after leading names go parabolic, and the Nasdaq rose over 80% in 1999 after the summer 1998 pullback.

The unresolved issue is whether the scale of AI capex earns a worthwhile return. Barclays says this will not be answered cleanly this month or for several quarters, so investors will stay sensitive to every disappointment.

Barclays calls this a garden-variety correction like the two earlier in 2026, when earnings ultimately outweighed market concerns. It has been tactically neutral on risk for three weeks, now sees a mild relief rally as the most likely near-term outcome, and stays neutral duration with longer US rates near the low end of their range.

tension_points.bull_case: Years-long bull markets usually end after leading names go parabolic. After the summer 1998 pullback the Nasdaq rose over 80% in 1999. Compute demand still outpaces supply and earnings have stayed healthy, so Barclays sees a garden-variety correction.
tension_points.bear_case: The scale of AI capex and its return remain unresolved. Google and Amazon free cash flow disappointed, Intel guided far below consensus, and investors will stay sensitive to every slight disappointment for several quarters.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Previous tech cycles collapsed when supply of compute overwhelmed demand, so evidence of that would undermine the bullish read.
